newsitem.title: UK: UK confirms Stagecoach/P'brook bid criteria.
newsitem.headline: UK confirms Stagecoach/P'brook bid criteria.

text.p: Britain's Department of Trade and Industry confirmed on Friday that it would only permit bus and passenger trains operator Stagecoach Holdings' planned acquisition of train leasor Porterbrook Leasing Co if Stagecoach complies with a number of pro-competition conditions.
Stagecoach had previously received notice of the likely criteria, and has already said it would put in place all the measures required.

DTI minister John Taylor said he planned to refer the deal to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission (MMC) unless suitable legally-binding undertakings were obtained from Stagecoach, an international bus and train operator.
"I agree with the Director General of Fair Trading (DGFT) that the merger gives rise to concerns in relation to the competitive process in the railway industry," he said.

Taylor's statement said the DGFT recommended that the undertakings should address principles of non-discrimination, confidentiality, cross-subsidy, co-operation with train operating companies (TOCs) and separate reports and accounting.
The concerns arose because, by July when it bid about 476 million stg for Porterbrook, Stagecoach had already taken control of one of Britain's 25 TOCs, under the ongoing privatisation process.
Regulators were concerned that Porterbrook, as one of just three such leasing companies in the UK sector, should continue to deal with all of the TOCs without any discrimination.
Stagecoach made clear in comments at the time of its bid, and in undertakings to the Office of Passenger Rail Franchising (OPRAF), that it would ring-fence Porterbrook.
Stagecoach shares rose 2.0p to 567-1/2p in midday trade.
